Run multivariate feature-based GSEA using limma and Hallmark gene sets

compute_factor_gsea.Rd

This function fits a multivariate linear model for each gene using all features in scores as continuous covariates (each feature standardized, and the cohort added when batch is given). For each feature, it extracts the moderated t-statistics and p-values, ranks genes, and performs GSEA (fgsea) using the human Hallmark gene sets from MSigDB. Optional dotplots for the top enriched pathways can be saved as PDFs.

Usage

compute_factor_gsea(
  counts_norm,
  scores,
  return = TRUE,
  top_n = 10,
  file_name = NULL,
  width = 8,
  height = 10,
  batch = NULL,
  seed = 123
)

Arguments

counts_norm

A numeric matrix or data frame of log-normalized gene expression values (e.g. log2(TPM + 1); genes as rows, gene symbols as row names, samples as columns).

scores

A data frame of continuous features (samples in rows, features in columns) to be modeled as covariates. Rows must be the same samples, in the same order, as the columns of counts_norm (checked by name; an error is raised otherwise). Features without variation are left out with a message.

return

Logical; if TRUE, generates and saves dotplots of top enriched Hallmark pathways for each feature. Default is TRUE.

top_n

Integer; number of top pathways to display in the dotplot. Default is 10.

file_name

Character; optional suffix for saved PDF files (Results/GSEA_<feature>_<file_name>.pdf, or Results/GSEA_<feature>.pdf without it). Default is NULL.

width

Numeric; width of the PDF plot in inches. Default is 8.

height

Numeric; height of the PDF plot in inches. Default is 10.

batch

Optional vector with the cohort of each sample (in the row order of scores, or named by sample). With two or more cohorts, the cohort is added to the model as a categorical covariate, so that expression differences between cohorts are not attributed to the features. Default NULL.

seed

Integer. Random seed used by fgsea::fgsea() (its p-values come from random permutations), so that the results are reproducible. Default 123. The caller's random number generator state is not changed.

Value

A list containing:

DE_results

A named list of topTable results for each feature, including logFC (change in expression per standard deviation of the feature), moderated t-statistics, p-values, and adjusted p-values.

GSEA_results

A named list of fgsea::fgsea() result tables (columns include pathway, pval, padj, NES) for each feature, ordered by p-value. fgsea may not be able to estimate the p-value of some pathways: their pval, padj and NES are then NA (their ES is kept).

Details

The function works as follows:

  1. Hallmark gene sets are retrieved from MSigDB using msigdbr.

  2. A multivariate linear model is fitted for each gene using limma::lmFit: all the features are in the same model, so the effect of each feature is adjusted for the others (and for the cohort with batch).

  3. Empirical Bayes moderation is applied via limma::eBayes.

  4. For each feature:

    1. Differential expression results are extracted using topTable for the coefficient of that feature.

    2. Genes are ranked by moderated t-statistics.

    3. Hallmark GSEA is performed on the ranked gene list with fgsea::fgsea().

    4. Optionally, a dotplot of the top enriched pathways is generated.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
  results <- compute_factor_gsea(counts_norm = expression_matrix,
                              scores = feature_table,
                              return = TRUE,
                              top_n = 10,
                              file_name = "Feature1_vs_all")
} # }
